title: Decision Time: AI and our Nuclear Arsenal
summary: A Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists panel weighs the benefits and risks of putting AI into nuclear command and control, including LLM escalation, hallucination and the 2025 UN resolution on human control.

assertions.quote: You see something then another country will be reacting to that and then it's a spiral that we could not be able to control.

verdicts.note: XPT forecasters reached no consensus on how AI would affect nuclear risk: some saw AI using or spreading nuclear weapons, others AI imposing arms control, and others thought AI would never be given control of nuclear weapons.

SIPRI says AI in nuclear command, control and communications raises concerns over reliability, transparency and oversight, and drives false-positive and false-negative risks that could raise the risk of inadvertent escalation.

RAND says an AI decision-support adviser could raise stability by reducing human error if proven effective, but many experts feared it could be fielded before it was robust or be subverted by hacking, poisoned data or manipulated inputs.

CNAS says integrating AI, autonomy or automation into nuclear command, early warning and delivery poses unique risks because of the extreme consequences of accidents, and quotes the head of the DoD's AI centre refusing AI in nuclear command; expert analysis, not data.

WEF warns that traditional deterrence may not hold when algorithms act before leaders can, and that with AI entering some nuclear command, control and communications functions these risks become critical; it frames a risk, not a measured increase.

The Bulletin's 2026 statement says AI in command and control may be problematic, especially in nuclear command and control, and that heavy dependence on black-box systems could be a serious danger even with a human in the loop; an expert board's judgment, not a measured effect.

assertions.quote: these large language models have a tendency to escalate very rapidly in terms of crisis

verdicts.note: Several war-game studies of current models found escalation bias and frequent nuclear use, though simulations differ from real command systems.
SIPRI reports that multiple studies and war games found LLMs could speed up decisions and contribute directly to escalation or nuclear use (citing Rivera et al. 2024).

assertions.quote: the unmitigated potential for hallucinations across large language models

verdicts.note: Current language models still produce confident false outputs at rates no nuclear decision system could accept.
SIPRI notes doubts that LLM-based systems can give sound decision support in rapid, high-stakes scenarios, but cites data scarcity and opacity rather than hallucination rates.

The Bulletin cites lingering concerns about LLM accuracy and their tendency to hallucinate and warns against heavy dependence on black-box systems in nuclear command and control, but stops short of saying they cannot be trusted.

assertions.quote: we came you know really quite close to nuclear war because early machines inappropriately detected launches.
it increases perceptions of deterrence among the general population.

verdicts.note: The evidence is a few survey experiments by one research group; it has not been widely replicated.

assertions.quote: They've really stalled in their modernization.

verdicts.note: Sarmat, new bombers and some submarines are years late, but Russia reports most of its strategic forces already modernized.

SIPRI says Russia's nuclear modernization is facing challenges (another failed Sarmat test in 2025, sanctions and war demands) but also reports a claimed successful Burevestnik test and a new Oreshnik base in Belarus, so troubled rather than stalled.

assertions.quote: human control and oversight must be maintained.
they were very clear in stating that there needed to be humans in control when it came to to nuclear weapons.

verdicts.note: SIPRI records that Xi Jinping and Joe Biden affirmed at their November 2024 meeting the need to keep human control over the decision to use nuclear weapons.

The White House readout of the 16 November 2024 Lima meeting states the two leaders affirmed the need to maintain human control over the decision to use nuclear weapons; this is the US account, China published its own separately.

assertions.quote: Mexicicoled resolution on AI command control and communication systems which was adopted by the UN General Assembly in 2025.

verdicts.note: The panel's diplomat co-authored the 2025 resolution; its exact wording on human control varied during negotiation.

assertions.quote: today we have lethal autonomous weapon systems that can really go uh the extra mile

verdicts.note: SIPRI says Ukraine used AI-guided drones with target recognition at scale in 2024-25 to hit Russian radars and bombers, but it also says no autonomous nuclear system is thought to be in operation and does not show drones picking their own targets.

assertions.quote: at a time when we are in a postarm arms control world.
